full_description: About The Company A high-growth foundation model startup headquartered in San Jose, California, operating at the intersection of two major platform shifts: foundation models and robotics. The company is building the Claude Code for Physical AI: a robotic foundation model plus a physical agentic framework for reliable, long-horizon operations in industrial environments. It delivers semi-humanoid robots as a workforce for industrial applications. Their Robots combine a robotic foundation model, force-aware manipulation, long-horizon reasoning, step-by-step execution verified against real operating procedures, and human-in-the-loop autonomy. The robot plans the job, executes each step, checks their work, and when it isn’t certain it doesn't guess—it escalates. About The Team The team includes experienced executives and AI leaders from leading global technology companies across robotics, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, automotive, and enterprise technology. Why join now You’ll be among the first engineers in the India team of a Silicon Valley deep tech startup. You’ll work on the same problems, with the same bar, as our team in San Jose. The India team is a core part of how we build models, data, and infrastructure, and you’ll own real pieces of the stack from your first quarter. Here you’ll own significant components, work across the whole stack, contribute at the cutting edge, see your code move a robot, and grow as fast as the company does. full_description: Job Summary This role is responsible for designing, developing, securing, and operating enterprise-grade web applications across both frontend and backend technologies. Lead the design and delivery of complex features and services using React, Python, GraphQL, and relational databases, balancing user needs, maintainability, performance, and delivery constraints. Define and evolve GraphQL schemas and resolver patterns; guide API compatibility, authorization, caching, pagination, and query performance decisions. Guide threat-aware design and production readiness, including access-control boundaries, sensitive-data handling, failure behavior, capacity, performance, and recovery considerations.
